physical_registration_requirements: Fresh unique label, tables, output and attempt identities
Source/model/code hashes; exact SQL/mapping/initial and final state rules
Unused chronological source-family roles including history/overlap purge
Explicit current UTC start/SQL/deadline cutoffs; no resurrection of expired protocols
Primary objective, practical margin, sample size/precision and guardrails justified from development
All original raw/publication/task/counter/correctness gates plus prospective SQL attribution
Failure wrapper, ntfy, detached ownership, logs/PID/check time; no duplicate executor
No run or model can be accepted from this programme or a generated design alone

experiments.title: Recover and freeze the evidence inventory
experiments.question: Which results, processes, sources and tests actually exist, and which source windows are already consumed?
experiments.intervention: Read current local and worker3 state when available. Inventory input hashes, snapshots, family use, frozen code and every failed/unattempted arm. No SQL or replay.
experiments.held_fixed: All historical result statuses and raw bytes. The November 1 failed campaign remains 0 passed / 1 failed / 1 unattempted.
experiments.evidence: Git/process inventory; signed source/consumption map; raw-copy SHA receipts; explicit unknowns.
experiments.continue_if: Repository state, evidence paths and source roles agree; no competing physical executor.
experiments.stop_if: Remote state is unknown, evidence is missing, or another scientific executor owns the server. Continue documentation only.

experiments.title: Repair prospective SQL ownership and terminal evidence
experiments.question: Can every completed marked SQL call be linked to its actual SQL execution, jobs, stages and successful task attempts without guessing?
experiments.intervention: Add a versioned SQL REST archive to the prospective collector. Resolve exact marked SQL and explicit success/running/failed job lists; preserve all observed engine jobs for the foreign-work census. Capture before retention loss and before post-run validation SQL.
experiments.held_fixed: Existing freshness, telemetry coverage, raw publication, terminal capture, task-attempt, correctness and multiset gates; old failed episodes; verified SF10 source and six SQL templates.
experiments.evidence: Saved genuine 463-call diagnostic as regression evidence; terminal SQL/job/stage/task receipts for one fresh control and one fresh maintenance episode; independent counter-presence audit.
experiments.continue_if: Both fresh episodes pass every original gate plus direct ownership coverage, input hashes and terminal raw mirroring.
experiments.stop_if: Any missing or ambiguous link, adverse counter, incomplete task attempt, capture gap or audit failure. Diagnose and register a mechanism change before another physical attempt.

experiments.title: Measure repeatability with null controls
experiments.question: How much do response time and collection overhead drift without compaction or policy changes?
experiments.intervention: Run two fresh-table no-maintenance replicas per development source block, alternating early/late position across a bounded four-block engineering pilot.
experiments.held_fixed: Rows, mapped arrivals, SQL sequence, layouts, client concurrency, engine configuration, observer and warmup. No cache flush or service restart.
experiments.evidence: Full-cohort response, service, generator lateness, queue area, CPU/I/O availability, wall time and host context for all eight episodes; paired null differences.
experiments.continue_if: Complete auditable runs and a measured variance/drift estimate sufficient to choose later precision and meaningful-effect criteria.
experiments.stop_if: Differences remain dominated by observer stalls or uncontrolled host changes. Fix measurement; do not use four blocks as a publication sample-size guarantee.

experiments.title: Measure the static layout response curve
experiments.question: Does changing file granularity improve the queries we actually execute, and where does reduced parallelism offset file-opening savings?
experiments.intervention: Prepare the same verified SF10 rows into three preregistered physical layouts, provisionally 16/64/256 files, with actual file-size distributions recorded. Execute identical queries without concurrent maintenance.
experiments.held_fixed: Data content and ordering recipe, compression, row-group settings, partition/sort rules, query parameters and resource configuration. Rotate layout order; use fresh tables.
experiments.evidence: Per-query and full-cohort response, scan tasks/bytes, planning evidence where available, actual file distributions and logical equality. Record successful achieved counts; never pretend requested count equals actual count.
experiments.continue_if: A reproducible useful region or a well-measured non-monotonic curve exists; select the layout range on development only.
experiments.stop_if: No plausible query benefit beyond repeatability, or layouts cannot be matched except for the intended intervention. Avoid training a predictor of a nonexistent benefit.

experiments.title: Isolate query sensitivity to layout
experiments.question: Which query mechanisms are sensitive to file granularity: selective scans, full scans, joins or aggregations?
experiments.intervention: First analyze the registered six real SQL templates separately on the same layout experiment. Add a separately registered richer query suite only after the initial mechanism is understood.
experiments.held_fixed: Arrival counts/order within each comparison and exact query parameter sets. Do not simultaneously change data scale, selectivity, join count and concurrency.
experiments.evidence: Query/plan identities; scan, exchange, join and aggregate counts; measured per-template effects and uncertainty across blocks; a workload-weighted effect using a declared mix.
experiments.continue_if: Specific sensitive and insensitive query classes can be explained with physical evidence, including any slowdowns.
experiments.stop_if: Only a selected favorable template improves and aggregate effects disappear. Restrict the claim or revise the workload question prospectively.

experiments.title: Separate transient interference from permanent layout benefit
experiments.question: Does maintenance execution overlap actually slow foreground work, separately from the new layout becoming visible?
experiments.intervention: Use fresh matched tables and snapshot-pinned foreground reads of the original layout during control and rewrite episodes. Record actual overlapping task intervals. In a separate phase compare compacted reads without maintenance.
experiments.held_fixed: Original read snapshot, query cohort, engine capacity, observer and arrival timing during the interference contrast. Snapshot pinning is diagnostic; production-like latest-snapshot semantics are evaluated separately.
experiments.evidence: Query task overlap, client-pending state, rewrite job CPU/I/O, response decomposition and actual commit/snapshot timestamps. Both no-overlap and overlap observations retained.
experiments.continue_if: A repeatable transient interference signal exists in a supported regime, or evidence establishes that it is too small to justify a separate interference model.
experiments.stop_if: A-minus-B estimates merely combine layout/cache/time changes; no direct overlap proof; or observed slowdown is entirely dispatch/evidence overhead.

experiments.title: Establish a useful start-time decision
experiments.question: Can choosing a different compaction start reduce full-cohort response while completing the same maintenance obligation?
experiments.intervention: Compare fixed early, midpoint and post-arrival starts on identical offered cohorts; default proposed offsets 0, H/2 and H, with H=1200s only if a new registration justifies retaining it. All arms must complete one equivalent rewrite and all foreground queries.
experiments.held_fixed: Initial physical layout, source window, SQL sequence, target layout rule, resources and observer. Include actual submission lag; intent time is not execution time.
experiments.evidence: Three-way paired response, queue area, p95/p99, drain, CPU/I/O and final maintenance state. A no-maintenance arm may be a separate diagnostic, never an equal-obligation winner.
experiments.continue_if: Start-time effects exceed development drift and the preregistered practical threshold; the sign/regime is interpretable across development blocks.
experiments.stop_if: Timing has no resolvable effect, or all timings are equivalent within the stated margin. Stop the forecast/ML chain in this regime.

experiments.title: Screen the interactions that can explain timing benefit
experiments.question: Does the useful timing choice depend jointly on natural demand regime, fragmentation and query mechanism?
experiments.intervention: Run a bounded 2x2x2x2 screen: lower/higher verified fragmentation, lower/higher natural-load source strata, lighter/heavier declared query mix and early/deferred start. Use intact real arrivals; select strata from development source descriptors, not observed winners.
experiments.held_fixed: SF10, same engine/resources, one client and fixed target-file rule. Load is a sampled source regime, not a randomized manipulated factor; report its association and interactions accordingly.
experiments.evidence: All 16 planned cells per replication set, actual source-family map and counterbalanced order, effect plots for timing-by-layout, timing-by-load and timing-by-query mix.
experiments.continue_if: A small number of repeatable interactions support a narrow timing hypothesis and a restricted feature set.
experiments.stop_if: Interactions are dominated by noise, incomplete cells or unrealistic saturation. Do not expand to an unrestricted Cartesian product.

experiments.title: Account for the whole observer and controller overhead
experiments.question: How much of measured response and CPU comes from feature acquisition, logging, durable publication, model inference and planning?
experiments.intervention: Instrument non-overlapping controller spans and process counters; compare two semantically equivalent implementation paths only where every evidence guarantee is retained. Reuse the completed SF1 inference diagnostic as historical context, not a whole-controller estimate.
experiments.held_fixed: Real queries, physical layout, logging durability and cadence, telemetry gates, model outputs and policy decisions in an implementation comparison.
experiments.evidence: Cold load versus warm inference, cache hits/misses, EXPLAIN/metadata calls, serialization/fsync, CPU-core-seconds, bytes and total client/engine time. Report inclusive/exclusive boundaries explicitly.
experiments.continue_if: End-to-end overhead is measured and small relative to the useful action effect, or an engineering optimization reduces it without changing semantics.
experiments.stop_if: A claimed gain exists only after subtracting guessed overhead or weakening collection. Keep the gain as observer engineering if policy is unchanged.

experiments.title: Build resource accounting before claiming efficiency
experiments.question: Can total CPU and I/O for the same work be measured without double counting?
experiments.intervention: Capture disjoint process/JVM CPU counters with process start identities, and scoped physical I/O where available, across collection, drain, maintenance and validation phases.
experiments.held_fixed: Same hardware, completed requests and rewrite obligation. Task CPU is a breakdown inside JVM CPU, not another quantity to add.
experiments.evidence: Counter availability/reset audit, accounting boundary, host interference log, summed CPU core-seconds, logical scan/rewrite bytes, physical I/O and observer costs in separate columns.
experiments.continue_if: Counters cover all relevant processes/phases with explicit scope and unchanged workload completion.
experiments.stop_if: Only CPU percent or unscoped host/device counters are available. Report those as diagnostics and do not infer CPU work, energy or cost savings.

experiments.title: Establish strong cheap policies
experiments.question: How much can a simple current-state rule achieve without any learned prediction?
experiments.intervention: Implement fixed early, fixed deadline and reactive queue/load threshold policies with bounded deferral, hysteresis and identical rewrite eligibility. Tune the reactive threshold on development only.
experiments.held_fixed: Same trigger opportunity, action set, target layout, deadline, resource budget and measurement path; enforce natural completion and record misses.
experiments.evidence: Physical paired full-cohort outcomes and overhead versus fixed starts. Report every threshold tried on development and freeze the chosen baseline before test.
experiments.continue_if: The strongest cheap baseline is selected transparently and reproducibly.
experiments.stop_if: A baseline is deliberately weak, misses its maintenance obligation, uses a different action set or is tuned on held-out data.

experiments.title: Test whether forecast information changes useful decisions
experiments.question: Does knowing near-future demand help beyond current queue/load state?
experiments.intervention: Use one planner and empirical costs with reactive/no forecast, last-window persistence, historical seasonal rate and a separately labelled perfect-arrival-information diagnostic. The oracle may use only the benchmark arrival future, not unseen physical cost outcomes.
experiments.held_fixed: Planner, action set, costs, cadence, overhead accounting and real offered arrivals. No retiming, thinning or stochastic synthetic demand substitution.
experiments.evidence: Forecast count errors, exact decision disagreements, supported horizons, physical response/obligation outcomes and oracle scope.
experiments.continue_if: Forecast information changes decisions and the physical outcomes improve beyond the cheap baseline; then justify learning C.
experiments.stop_if: Good forecast scores do not change decisions, or even the diagnostic oracle has little useful action margin in the evaluated regime.

experiments.title: Test learned costs against empirical costs
experiments.question: Does a learned latency estimate improve decisions beyond query/layout medians?
experiments.intervention: Compare train-only query median, query/layout median, conditional median, log Ridge and a small boosted-tree candidate under the same whole-family splits. Use the same planner to test the selected candidate against medians.
experiments.held_fixed: Training population, feature availability, held-out queries, forecast, planner and per-candidate tuning budget. Saved October models/tests remain consumed.
experiments.evidence: All-row coverage, common-support equal-episode errors, supported decision disagreements, warm/cold overhead and independent physical policy contrasts.
experiments.continue_if: The candidate contributes a repeatable net policy benefit on fresh families beyond the best inexpensive estimator.
experiments.stop_if: Prediction MAE improves but decisions or measured outcomes do not; unsupported states dominate; cost exceeds decision value. Retain the simpler estimator.

experiments.title: Decide whether separate A/B models are necessary
experiments.question: Is separate conditional fitting more useful than a shared model with maintenance state?
experiments.intervention: Compare a shared model plus state/interactions against separate A/B models; include shared-model and separate-model variants under matched total tuning/parameter budgets where possible.
experiments.held_fixed: Same query/layout overlap support, complete history, source-family roles, outcome definition and cost model family.
experiments.evidence: Counts of independent episodes and overlap exposure per state; conditional and common-support errors; capacity/training time; physical decision contribution.
experiments.continue_if: Separate models add reproducible supported value, with enough independent maintenance episodes and matched layout support.
experiments.stop_if: A has only sparse rows from a few episodes or differs systematically in layout. Do not interpret A-minus-B as a causal penalty.

experiments.title: Estimate rewrite duration and layout transition
experiments.question: Can the controller estimate rewrite work and completion time from pre-action state?
experiments.intervention: Collect real isolated rewrites over supported file-count/size layouts, then matched concurrent-load rewrites. Compare empirical medians, bytes/throughput regression and a small learned regressor.
experiments.held_fixed: Rewrite algorithm/options, logical rows, hardware and pre-action feature boundary. Separate no-op/failed rewrites from successful useful transitions.
experiments.evidence: Actual client duration, rewritten/added files and bytes, final layout, commit time, CPU/I/O and concurrent demand context.
experiments.continue_if: Enough independent rewrites support the chosen model and useful duration/transition error bounds.
experiments.stop_if: Only a handful of repeated rewrites exist or model predicts file reduction as if it were response benefit. Keep empirical support limited.

experiments.title: Remove unnecessary features and tune within development
experiments.question: Which features and model settings earn their acquisition and fitting cost?
experiments.intervention: Nested development comparisons: SQL identity; plus layout; plus observed queue/state; plus plan operators; plus complete host windows. Compare small fixed hyperparameter grids, not unrestricted search.
experiments.held_fixed: Whole source-family folds, targets, transformations, scoring/coverage rule and tuning budget. Expensive plan features must be timed/cached with snapshot binding.
experiments.evidence: Per-feature-group incremental predictive and decision value, acquisition time, OOD rate and chosen hyperparameters with trial ledger.
experiments.continue_if: Retain only groups whose net benefit survives development checks; freeze before final evaluation.
experiments.stop_if: Feature availability leaks future outcomes; row-wise cross-validation; test-driven tuning; complexity without measurable decision value.

experiments.title: Calibrate uncertainty only with adequate blocks
experiments.question: Do uncertainty estimates support safer timing decisions on genuinely separate calibration blocks?
experiments.intervention: Freeze models; calibrate block-level residual scores on unused calibration families and evaluate once on separate test families. Define whether coverage concerns a block maximum, an episode aggregate or an individual query.
experiments.held_fixed: Model fit, calibration definition, decision horizon, target units, source grouping and declared risk. Never apply an individual-query interval to whole-episode guarantees.
experiments.evidence: Finite conformal rank, number of calibration blocks, empirical coverage/width, OOD refusals and dependence/shift limitations.
experiments.continue_if: The mathematical rank is finite and the independently chosen statistical/precision requirements are met; physical benefit of the uncertainty rule is demonstrated.
experiments.stop_if: Too few blocks, dependence, shifted support or calibration/test reuse. Keep outputs explicitly uncalibrated; nine blocks for 90% is a rank minimum, not adequate power.

experiments.title: Isolate the value of C, learned costs and uncertainty
experiments.question: Which component causes the policy improvement?
experiments.intervention: Use a fixed planner in a 2x2 ablation: persistence versus selected forecast, empirical versus selected learned costs. Add uncertainty on/off only after E16. Keep the strongest reactive policy outside this 2x2 as a required comparator.
experiments.held_fixed: Action set, invocation cadence, training source, terminal obligation, physical layouts, workload and resource budget.
experiments.evidence: Four-cell paired physical comparison on fresh development blocks; marginal and interaction effects; total overhead. Later optional eight-cell uncertainty extension.
experiments.continue_if: At least one justified component adds useful outcome value with stable support and accounting.
experiments.stop_if: A better result is attributable to a different planner/action set or ignored overhead. Simplify components that do not add value.

experiments.title: Freeze and execute the one-time confirmatory comparison
experiments.question: Does the frozen selected method beat the frozen strongest baseline in the declared target population?
experiments.intervention: Preregister primary metric, practical effect, precision/sample size, family split/purge, arm order, failure policy and guardrails from development. Run complete matched physical blocks on untouched families once.
experiments.held_fixed: All model artifacts, baseline thresholds, feature code, planner, hardware definition, action rule and analysis script. No test feedback into model choice.
experiments.evidence: All attempts, full raw/audit manifests, equal-work contrasts, family-level intervals, raw distributions, response/resource/debt guardrails and sensitivity analyses marked secondary.
experiments.continue_if: The preregistered superiority/equivalence criterion and all safety/correctness/obligation gates are satisfied.
experiments.stop_if: Failure, imprecision, effect below practical threshold or guardrail violation. Report inconclusive/negative; consume test and design a genuinely new study if needed.

experiments.title: Optional CPU or I/O objective study
experiments.question: Can maintenance reduce resource work for the same completed workload without an unacceptable response regression?
experiments.intervention: Before new outcomes, register a distinct resource-first protocol: choose CPU core-seconds OR a well-scoped I/O metric as primary and a justified response constraint. Do not rename old response experiments.
experiments.held_fixed: Same offered/cohort work, full drain, successful rewrite and final-state criterion; all observer/controller cost included.
experiments.evidence: Resource-response Pareto plots with a fixed selected operating point, resource provenance and both positive and negative outcomes.
experiments.continue_if: Net savings survive equal-work accounting and the response constraint on fresh data.
experiments.stop_if: Savings arise from omitted requests/maintenance, lower quality, unmeasured processes or moving work outside the horizon.

experiments.title: Validate scale transfer to SF100
experiments.question: Does the mechanism survive a larger verified dataset?
experiments.intervention: Audit the actual SF100 source/generator and capacity, then repeat the smallest decisive comparison at SF100. First test frozen SF10 models; report retraining as a different adaptation experiment.
experiments.held_fixed: Query semantics, controlled layout treatment, policy interfaces and complete evidence gates. Do not change scale and engine/resources simultaneously.
experiments.evidence: All-table row/type/provenance checks, actual data bytes, full correctness, support coverage, resource/admission receipts and physical outcomes.
experiments.continue_if: Capacity and verification pass and the mechanism transfers or its failure is interpretable.
experiments.stop_if: Insufficient RAM/disk/evidence budget or no supported predictions. SF100 is an external-validity branch, not a cure for broken SF10 evidence.

experiments.title: Concurrency and query-mix transfer
experiments.question: Does the result hold beyond one serial client and a narrow mapped query mix?
experiments.intervention: Change client concurrency in one series (proposed 1 then 4); change query mix in a separate series. Use real mapped SQL and audit per-session queue/task ownership.
experiments.held_fixed: Everything except the one named factor. Preserve intact real arrival timing and expose over/underload rather than compressing the trace.
experiments.evidence: Aggregate and per-query response, per-session ledgers, engine overlap and logical results; policy support/refusals and utilization.
experiments.continue_if: Mechanism persists or a clear saturation boundary can be reported.
experiments.stop_if: Concurrent request ownership/accounting cannot be proved or experiment mixes multiple interventions.

experiments.title: Add continuing fragmentation from real writes
experiments.question: Does timing matter more when a real table continues accumulating small files?
experiments.intervention: Register an actual write source with data lineage and ingestion timestamps. If using benchmark-generated inserts, label them explicitly as controlled benchmark writes, subject to user approval; they cannot be called production trace writes.
experiments.held_fixed: Equal committed writes, queries and maintenance debt across arms; consistent snapshot/visibility semantics.
experiments.evidence: Committed row/version history, write latency, query response, file/debt trajectory, rewrite work and conflict outcomes.
experiments.continue_if: A real supported write source and complete correctness boundary exist; ongoing debt creates a useful timing tradeoff.
experiments.stop_if: No authorized write provenance or missing data. Do not invent ingestion from Snowset arrival timestamps.

experiments.title: Selective or incremental file-group compaction
experiments.question: Can bounded useful work reduce the disturbance of a monolithic rewrite?
experiments.intervention: Compare whole eligible rewrite with a registered subset/file-group strategy through supported Iceberg options; preserve identical long-run obligation and record every commit.
experiments.held_fixed: Same data, workload, final maintenance obligation and target size; no preemption/cancellation of active jobs.
experiments.evidence: Per-action duration/work, interference episodes, accumulated debt, total CPU/I/O and final layout.
experiments.continue_if: Smaller actions improve the declared objective after total-work accounting and repeated action overhead.
experiments.stop_if: Partial compaction wins only by leaving debt, changing target quality or hiding extra commits/rewrite amplification.

experiments.title: Partition prioritization
experiments.question: Which partition should receive a fixed maintenance budget first?
experiments.intervention: Register multiple real partitions and measured query access frequencies; compare round-robin, file-count priority, workload-aware empirical priority and a supported learned ranking.
experiments.held_fixed: Total budget, eligible partition set, action implementation and final obligation rule; isolate selection from timing.
experiments.evidence: Partition-level response exposure, maintenance bytes, fairness/debt and end-to-end performance.
experiments.continue_if: Selection causes useful effects beyond a strong cheap ranking with no starvation.
experiments.stop_if: Only one unpartitioned table exists, missing access provenance or comparison conflates a larger budget with smarter selection.

experiments.title: Delete-file maintenance and merge-on-read
experiments.question: Does a different, real maintenance debt produce a stronger measurable read/write tradeoff?
experiments.intervention: Register actual deletes/updates and supported Iceberg delete semantics in fresh isolated tables. Compare appropriate delete/data maintenance actions; this is a new hypothesis.
experiments.held_fixed: Identical logical changes and snapshot correctness, action eligibility and final deletion semantics.
experiments.evidence: Delete-file inventory, row/result equality, read amplification, commit/conflict work and response/resource accounting.
experiments.continue_if: Debt and outcomes are directly evidenced with complete correctness.
experiments.stop_if: Deletes are fabricated, semantics differ between arms or the implementation cannot attribute merge work.

experiments.title: Second environment or engine
experiments.question: How much of the result depends on one machine or Spark implementation?
experiments.intervention: Replicate the minimal decisive experiment on a second available resource configuration or engine. Change one environment dimension per registered study.
experiments.held_fixed: Logical dataset, query semantics, workload family selection and maintenance objective; disclose unavoidable engine semantic differences.
experiments.evidence: Hardware/software configuration, version pins, compatibility/correctness checks and paired effects within each environment.
experiments.continue_if: Result transfers, or a clear engine/resource limitation is established.
experiments.stop_if: A new environment is unavailable or changes so many factors that the study cannot explain the difference.

experiments.title: Delta Lake external-validity branch
experiments.question: Does the same timing principle extend to another table format?
experiments.intervention: Implement a separate Delta adapter for native bin-packing OPTIMIZE, using verified logical rows and equivalent queries; retain its format-specific snapshots and metrics.
experiments.held_fixed: Within-format resource and workload comparison; same high-level question. Never treat OPTIMIZE and Iceberg rewrite as identical implementations.
experiments.evidence: Correctness/provenance, adapter audit, native maintenance output and equal-obligation comparisons.
experiments.continue_if: The mechanism is already credible on Iceberg and extra engineering can answer a specific transfer question.
experiments.stop_if: Switching formats is only an attempt to find a favorable number or required native instrumentation is absent.

experiments.title: Hudi merge-on-read branch
experiments.question: Does the timing hypothesis apply to log-to-base-file merging under continuing updates?
experiments.intervention: Build a separate Hudi MOR experiment with actual updates and read/write visibility checks. Hudi compaction merges log updates; it is not the same as file-size bin packing.
experiments.held_fixed: Equal real update streams, read semantics, base/log debt and completed maintenance.
experiments.evidence: Log/base inventories, read amplification, update latency, merge work and full workload outcomes.
experiments.continue_if: A supported MOR workload and a distinct research question justify the larger adapter effort.
experiments.stop_if: No update source or no equivalent work/semantics; this is a project pivot, not an immediate fallback.

experiments.title: RocksDB/LSM pivot
experiments.question: Is a fundamentally different maintenance architecture necessary for a new hypothesis?
experiments.intervention: Only after an explicit project decision, move to a fresh LSM research problem and compare appropriate native baselines such as workload-aware compaction methods.
experiments.held_fixed: New scope, actual supported key/value workload provenance and native latency/debt metrics; do not transfer lakehouse claims automatically.
experiments.evidence: New literature review, workload, correctness/accounting adapter and baseline reproductions.
experiments.continue_if: The new mechanism and available time justify a separate project trajectory.
experiments.stop_if: The motivation is simply that Iceberg had a null result. Existing strong LSM literature makes this an expensive pivot.

experiments.title: Robustness, drift and unsupported states
experiments.question: When does the controller lose support, miss a deadline or make a harmful decision?
experiments.intervention: Evaluate preregistered real workload shifts, unseen layouts and model age on separate data. Measure natural failures; do not deliberately corrupt evidence or kill jobs.
experiments.held_fixed: Frozen model/decision policy and transparent refusal contract.
experiments.evidence: Coverage/refusal rates, worst blocks, deadline/debt violations and a failure taxonomy with raw receipts.
experiments.continue_if: Scope and operating limits are explicit; conclusions survive stated robustness checks.
experiments.stop_if: Unsupported predictions silently fall back, metrics exclude failed arms or drift triggers test-set retuning.

experiments.title: Write and release a reproducible paper artifact
experiments.question: Can a reader reconstruct every figure and verify the central claim?
experiments.intervention: Freeze the claim ledger, source versions, all attempts, analysis commands and raw manifests; write methods/results/limitations and package a bounded reproducible artifact.
experiments.held_fixed: Primary outcome and failure history; no selective removal of null or contradictory experiments.
experiments.evidence: Paper tables/figures with source SHA links, environment/seed records, costs, data-license notes and next-agent instructions.
experiments.continue_if: The central claim is supported, baseline comparison is fair, artifact reproduces and the team/guide review the venue fit.
experiments.stop_if: Only screenshots, prediction accuracy or a single favorable run support the claim. Target acceptance is never guaranteed.

experiments.title: Boundary or negative-result research branch
experiments.question: Under what conditions is compaction timing or a learned controller not worth its cost?
experiments.intervention: Preregister a bounded regime map and equivalence/practical-effect analysis on fresh blocks, retaining layout/parallelism and overhead mechanisms.
experiments.held_fixed: Fair baselines, equal completed work, sufficient precision and the same evidence quality as a positive claim.
experiments.evidence: Timing-effect intervals, useful-region boundaries, overhead-to-effect ratios and independent reproduction.
experiments.continue_if: A generalizable explanatory boundary with sufficiently precise evidence distinguishes the work from prior findings.
experiments.stop_if: Failure to reject zero is presented as equivalence, or a failed measurement pipeline is presented as a negative scientific finding.

experiments.title: Observer-efficiency engineering branch
experiments.question: Can durable evidence collection be made cheaper without changing the measured system contract?
experiments.intervention: Study publication/serialization/storage placement through semantically equivalent implementations; quantify the effect on an external control loop and workload.
experiments.held_fixed: Every required record, timestamp, durability, coverage, checksum and failure gate. Freeze policy outputs for implementation comparisons.
experiments.evidence: Raw-equivalence proofs, latency/CPU/write costs, drift controls, end-to-end effects and independent workloads.
experiments.continue_if: A distinct transferable mechanism and independent evidence support more than a one-machine storage-location observation.
experiments.stop_if: Claims rely only on the historical 31–42% observer-path contrast, omitted durability or assumed GIL causality.

null_repeatability.rationale: Two identical fresh-table replicates per source block estimate drift. Four block slots are a bounded engineering pilot, not power.

layout_curve.rationale: Fourfold steps around the existing 64-file SF10 preparation expose granularity effects while holding logical bytes constant. Counts require capability validation.

timing.rationale: Bracket early/transient/post-arrival choices; every arm completes the same rewrite and query cohort. Offsets bind to a separately registered horizon.

interaction_screen.rationale: 16-cell development screen for timing interactions. Natural load is source-stratified, not randomly assigned or synthetically scaled.

policy_ablation.rationale: Four cells isolate forecast information and cost modeling under identical planner/actions. Strong reactive comparator is added separately.

uncertainty_ablation.rationale: Optional eight cells only after E16; uncalibrated estimates cannot fill calibrated_block_rule.

scope_cartesian_upper_bound.rationale: Explicit 29160-cell combinatorial cost illustration before repetitions. NOT a proposed campaign. Unsupported combinations remain plans and must not be launched.
